title: London Relocation Services
transcript:
Speaker 1: Daniel: London Relocation Services. Daniel speaking. How may I help you?
Speaker 2: Anna: Good morning. My family and I are moving to London later this year, and I wonder if you can help.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Sure. First of all, I’ll need to get some personal details. May I take your full name, please?
Speaker 2: Anna: It’s Anna Woods.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Thanks. Where are you moving from?
Speaker 2: Anna: Northern Ireland, just outside Belfast, actually.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Right. And what’s your current address?
Speaker 2: Anna: It’s 118 Fordyce Park. I’ll spell that for you. It’s F O R D Y C E, and that’s in Ballysillan.
Speaker 1: Daniel: And what’s the postcode?
Speaker 2: Anna: It’s BT149BJ.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Alright. And could I take a contact phone number?
Speaker 2: Anna: I’ll give you my mobile number, as you can get me on that anytime. It’s .
Speaker 1: Daniel: Great. Got that. Now we always like to get a bit more information about the families that we’re moving. It helps with the search. Are you moving for work?
Speaker 2: Anna: Yes. My husband’s just got a new job in London.
Speaker 1: Daniel: And what about you? Do you work?
Speaker 2: Anna: Well, I’ve been working as a teaching assistant recently, but I’m actually a qualified nurse, and I’d like to get back into that if possible.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Right. And do you have any children?
Speaker 2: Anna: Yes. A son. So we need to find a school for him.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Is it a secondary school you’ll be looking for?
Speaker 2: Anna: No. He’s still in primary school. He’s not quite at the secondary level yet.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Fine. So let’s go on to talk about your requirements for the property. Do you have a preferred location? Is your husband’s job in the center?
Speaker 2: Anna: No. It’s in East London, but we’d rather live somewhere quieter.
Speaker 0: Daniel: Sure.
Speaker 1: Daniel: There are some lovely areas in the South.
Speaker 2: Anna: Okay. That sounds great. Now my husband doesn’t want to spend too long commuting to work every day.
Speaker 1: Daniel: So I imagine that ideally, he’d like to be not too far from a station then.
Speaker 2: Anna: Yes. He drives now, but I guess that’s not going to be possible, and he’s not keen on buses.
Speaker 1: Daniel: What about you or your son? Do you have any preferences? Does your son do any sport, for example?
Speaker 2: Anna: He’s quite active, so I’m sure he’d love a park nearby to run around in. He doesn’t do swimming or anything like that.
Speaker 1: Daniel: So what sort of property do you have in mind?
Speaker 2: Anna: We have friends who live in an amazing flat over there. But as we’ve always lived in a house, I think we’ll stick with that. We’d find it hard to adapt to a flat.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Okay. And size-wise, how many bedrooms would you like?
Speaker 2: Anna: Well, there’s just myself, my husband, and our son.
Speaker 1: Daniel: So you definitely need a two bedroom property. But how about having a guest room? I might be able to find a three-bedroom property for you.
Speaker 2: Anna: Yes. That would be ideal. We’re sure to have family visiting often.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Alright. I’ve made a note of that. Now are there any other requirements for your new property?
Speaker 2: Anna: Well, it’s not essential, but it’d be handy to have an office for when my husband works from home. It doesn’t need to be a big one. I guess it all comes down to budget.
Speaker 1: Daniel: Yes. Okay, Anna. Well, I’ve certainly got enough to be getting on with, and I will—
